newsitem.title: UK: IPE gas oil closes $5.25 lower in line with U.S..
newsitem.headline: IPE gas oil closes $5.25 lower in line with U.S..

text.p: IPE gas oil futures last traded $5.25 a tonne down on Tuesday, the day's low, after the contract was driven lower by weaker U.S. heating oil, traders said.
The February contract finished at $203.75 a tonne in a late slide propelled earthwards by the NYMEX opening, after touching a high of $208.25 during the morning session.
"It's just pressure from heating oil in the States," said a trader.
The front-month March contract for Brent crude oil futures traded at $22.53 a barrel, down five cents, at 1807 GMT, after hitting an intra-day low of $22.32.
Traders said milder weather in Europe and the United States, combined with ample U.S. supplies, was pushing gas oil down.
"With lack of winter demand gas oil seems to be dithering and is now losing ground," one trader said.
This week's American Petroleum Institute data, delayed until Wednesday by a U.S. holiday on Monday, is expected to show heating oil stocks nearly up to last year's levels.
Last week's data showed heating oil stocks in the northeastern United States fell 390,000 barrels, but the year-on-year deficit narrowed by around half to 3.2 million barrels.
